spans.s: पूयमान—यवम् ind. at the time of winnowing barley g. तिष्ठद्ग्व्-आदि (cf. पूत-य्˚).
cl. 1. P. पू॑यति (TS.; ŚBr. &c.), Ā. पूयते (Dhātup. xiv, 13), to become foul or putrid, stink.

etym.s: [cf. Zd. pū, puiti; Gk. πύον, πύθω ; Lat. pūs, pūteo; Lith. púti; Goth. fûls; Germ. faul; Eng. foul.]

spans.s: n. purulent matter, pus, suppuration, discharge from an ulcer or wound, ŚBr.; &c.
पूय—भुज् mfn. eating purulent carcasses, Mn. xii, 72.
पूय—रक्त m. (sc. रोग) ‘having purulent blood’, a kind of disease of the nose with discharge of p˚ blood, Suśr.
पूय—वह m. ‘filthy-streamed’, N. of a partic. hell, VP.
पूय—शोणित n. purulent blood, ichor, Mn. iii, 180.
‘resembling pus’, a kind of bloody-flux, L.
‘hostile to suppuration’, the Nimb tree, Azadirachta Indica (the leaves of which are used to produce dispersion or absorption of p˚ matter), L.
a partic. disease of the place of junction (संधि) of the eye
suppuration at the joints, white swelling, Suśr.
‘having fetid wafer’, N. of a partic. hell (cf. पूय-वह).
pus, discharge from a wound or sore, L.
